notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase, general vs during-work for conduct rules such as data input, disclosure and accuracy checks; resolved by coding conduct rules by when the act happens and definitions/principles/scope as general. (2) unit_stance (not scored), permit vs require for disclosure duties (permit, since require means AI use is built into the work) and prohibit vs restrict (restrict for ban-unless-permitted or ban with an exception). (3) policy_type: bias-in-output rule (P53 over P31), research accuracy duty (P62 over P31), plagiarism item on AI passed off as own (P36 over P29). (4) Anchor length and policy wording: several anchors were cut mid-clause, so a normalized policy was written; one two-rule research sentence was split into two units (one extra unit, not counted as only-A or only-B). Only-A units kept: Madrid DPO approval, funders' peer-review prohibition. Only-B kept: disclosure-content sentence, Libraries contact, AI definition scope, staff data-sharing clause. Only-B dropped (6): two scope sentences in the Guidelines intro and four general procedure units in the Academic Integrity Policy (not AI-specific). Document stance agreed on all 3 documents.
